title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-22
content:
2026-03-03 - morning notes

Top of mind / goals for today:
- Validate dedicated pool capacity for AcmePilot (req: 16xA100, steady 600 tok/s) before Tuesday rollout.
- Follow up on node-level OOMs seen yesterday during long-run rnn batch tests.
- Prep small rolling restart plan for gpu-driver update (460->470) and test on canary (node-gpu-canary-02).
- Quick network check: confirm MTU and jumbo frames on eu-west-1 cluster for RDMA path.

Quick checklist (prioritized):
1) Capacity check - AcmePilot
   - Action: run capacity estimator script (scripts/capacity/estimate_acme.sh) with 95th pct request profile
   - Command: ./estimate_acme.sh --model=redwood-small --qps=50 --seq=1024
   - ETA: 45m; if > headroom threshold (20%), open JIRA to request extra reserved nodes (JIRA-ENG-4321)

2) Investigate yesterday's OOMs
   - Logs: /var/log/kubelet/gpu-ops.log and inference-runtime logs (s3://redwood-logs/prod/gpu/2026-03-02/)
   - Hypothesis: KV cache + long seq length causing mem spikes; maybe cache eviction not kicking in on heavy batching.
   - Quick checks: nvidia-smi, docker stats, kubectl top nodes/pods
   - Notes: Pod inference-worker-1 restarted 3x at 23:10; cgroup memory reported ~94% before kill.

3) GPU driver rollout (canary -> staggered)
   - Canary: node-gpu-canary-02 (eu-west-1a) today afternoon after smoke tests
   - Steps:
     a) drain node, cordon (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data)
     b) upgrade driver via ansible playbook: ansible-playbook playbooks/gpu-driver-upgrade.yml -i inventory/canary
     c) run smoke: run tests/inference_smoke.sh (check p50/p95 latency and mem)
     d) monitor 2h, then schedule 6x nodes in batch-1 if green
   - Rollback: reimage node from snapshot if kernel/driver mismatch 

4) Networking - RDMA & MTU
   - Reminder: eu-west-1 recently had MTU mismatch on eth1 on node pool-3. Re-run mtu-checker.
   - Command: sudo ip link set dev eth1 mtu 9000; /opt/tools/mtu-checker --nodes pool-3 --verify
   - Coordinate with networking (tag: @Priya) before mass changes.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider smaller kv-cache default for large-batch jobs (maybe 8MB -> 4MB) to reduce per-pod memory footprint. Test with synthetic load.
- Try enabling continuous-batching limiter for rnn workloads to keep per-request mem bounded. Add metric: batch_size_distribution in telemetry.
- Follow up on proposal to gate large sequence workloads behind quota or dedicated pool so they don't evict other customers. Draft in Confluence: infra/gpu-onboarding (linked).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- If dedicated pool for AcmePilot needs +4 nodes, do we pull from spot capacity or request more reserved? Cost/ops tradeoff. Ping finance for temporary approval?
- Is driver 470 fully validated for CUDA 11.8 stacks across all models? I saw one flaky fp16 run on 470 in canary last week. Need to reproduce.

Daily TODO (short):
- [ ] run capacity estimator for AcmePilot (slot: 9:30)
- [ ] triage OOM logs and post findings in #infra-gpu-ops (target: 11:30)
- [ ] canary driver upgrade (slot: 14:00)
- [ ] re-run mtu-checker on eu-west pool-3 and verify (slot: 16:00)
- [ ] add batch_size_distribution metric to telemetry backlog (create ticket)

Housekeeping:
- Reminder: update on-call runbook with new eviction thresholds (page: confluence:runbooks/gpu-eviction)
- If we escalate to SRE for rolling reimage, add cost estimate to incident note.

Random command snippets / useful locations:
- kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o wide
- kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -n
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 5
- logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/gpu/
- scripts: infra/scripts/gpu/*

End notes:
- Quick wins today = prevent AcmePilot capacity surprise and get canary driver upgrade done. Everything else is lower priority but document findings.
- Ping Priya for MTU change approval; Evan to help with canary verification.

-- Maya
